o: Count permutations of [1..n] where gcd(value, position) = 1 for every position. n ≤ 12 suggests bitmask DP: fill positions left to right, tracking which values are used. dp[mask] = number of ways to fill the first popcount(mask) positions using exactly the values in mask. Transition: place an unused value v at position i = popcount(mask)+1 if gcd(v, i) = 1. Example: n=3 gives 3.
k: Bitmask DP over used values; position is implied by popcount.
Prune heavily: positions with few coprime candidates cut the state space drastically.

a.i: Iterate masks in increasing order; for each reachable mask, try placing every unused coprime value at the next position.
s: For each mask, i = popcount(mask)+1; for each unused v with gcd(v,i)=1, add dp[mask] to dp[mask|bit(v)]
a.t: O(2ⁿ · n) with cheap gcd checks

a.i: Same state space explored top-down via recursion on (position, usedMask), memoized — often faster in practice because unreachable states are never touched.
s: Recurse(pos, mask): if pos > n return 1
Try each unused v with gcd(v,pos)=1, sum recursive results
Memoize on mask (pos is determined by mask)

w: Either version is fine; mention that answers fit in 32 bits for n ≤ 12 but intermediate Java/C++ sums are safest as long. Pitfall: positions are 1-indexed (position i ranges 1..n) and gcd(v, i) = 1 includes v = i only when both are 1. Follow-up: count permutations with gcd(a[i], i) > 1 instead (inclusion–exclusion territory).
